options.text: A 3D network of carbon atoms like diamond
A single layer of graphite, one atom thick, arranged in hexagons
A spherical molecule of 60 carbon atoms
A type of carbon nanotube

questions.explanation: Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice - essentially one layer of graphite. It is just one atom thick, making it the thinnest material known. Despite its thinness, it is incredibly strong, lightweight, and an excellent conductor of electricity due to delocalised electrons.

questions.stem: Buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀) is used to deliver drug molecules inside the body. Why is its hollow spherical structure useful for this?

options.text: It is magnetic and can be guided to specific organs
Drug molecules can be trapped inside the hollow cage and released at the target site
It dissolves easily in water
It has a very high melting point so it survives body temperature

questions.explanation: Buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀) has a hollow, cage-like spherical structure that can encapsulate drug molecules inside it. This allows drugs to be transported through the body and delivered to specific target sites. The cage structure protects the drug and can be designed to release it where needed.

questions.stem: Carbon nanotubes are used to reinforce sports equipment like tennis rackets. Which property makes them ideal for this?

options.text: They conduct electricity
They are excellent thermal insulators
They are extremely strong yet very lightweight
They are soft and flexible

questions.explanation: Carbon nanotubes have extraordinary tensile strength (they are incredibly strong for their weight) while being very lightweight. This combination makes them perfect for reinforcing composite materials in sports equipment, where strength without added weight is essential. They also conduct electricity and heat, but strength-to-weight ratio is the key property for reinforcement.

options.text: It contains metal atoms
Each carbon atom bonds to only 3 others, leaving one delocalised electron per atom
It contains ions that can move freely
It has a very large surface area

questions.explanation: Like graphite, each carbon atom in graphene forms 3 covalent bonds, using only 3 of its 4 outer electrons. The fourth electron from each carbon atom is delocalised across the entire sheet and can move freely to carry electrical charge. This makes graphene an excellent electrical conductor.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a potential application of graphene?

options.text: Flexible touchscreens for electronic devices
Thermal insulation for buildings
Ultra-fast electronic circuits
Lightweight but strong composite materials

questions.explanation: Graphene is an excellent thermal conductor, so it would be unsuitable for thermal insulation (which requires a poor conductor). Graphene's properties - electrical conductivity, strength, flexibility, and transparency - make it ideal for flexible screens, fast electronics, and strong composites. Its high thermal conductivity is actually useful for heat dissipation in electronics.
